answer: One island orchard slot per identity requires a 70-credit bond. It must board a harbor ferry and check in at the orchard gate in one ten-minute window; both logs must show the same key, or the bond burns. An auditor recomputes the window from both logs and voids duplicates or late keys. Ferry slots are scarce: the first costs 24 credits, the kth 24+4(k-1), so the 1000th costs 4020 and 1000 fakes pay 2,022,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-ferry ring fails because one operator cannot board 1000 distinct keys at once. An honest agent pays 24 once and recovers its bond if clean.
